statement_refuted: For a nonzero quadratic hub Q=dX^2+2XL+Y, an independent cap-one hub X, a bounded density of L, and a uniform square-root slice estimate mu_l(E)<=K|E|^{1/2} suffice by themselves for a universal bounded output density.
counterexample_summary: For any a>0 take independent X,U,Z uniform on [-1/2,1/2], L=U, Y=a^{-1}U^2-Z^2. Then ||p_L||_infinity=1 and every unnormalised L=l slice satisfies mu_l(E)<=2|E|^{1/2} for every measurable E, but Q=aX^2+2XU+Y=a(X+U/a)^2-Z^2 has logarithmically unbounded density. Its matrix spectrum is {a+a^{-1},0,-1}, so this is not a full-QFORM counterexample.
missing_factor: The scalar-pivot Schur complement S obeys det(M)=d det(S); under the three-large-eigenvalue target |det S|>=1/|d|. A valid near-null receiver must spend this determinant curvature together with original-product provenance before reducing to slice-only data.
partner_control: For Q_eta=aX^2+2XU+(a^{-1}+eta)U^2-Z^2, account02/B05 QFORM-NEARNULL-SCALAR-DEPENDENT-PAIR-v1 gives ||p||_infinity<=31|a eta|^{-1/6}. At a=1, eta=-2, the matrix spectrum is {sqrt(2),-sqrt(2),-1} and the bound is <27.618.
relation_to_existing_corrections: Strictly strengthens the interface lesson of QFORM-ONE-HEAVY-ROW-SAME-SQUARE-ABSORPTION-FALSE-v1 by retaining a uniform all-measurable-set square-root slice constant. Consistent with QFORM-CONDITIONAL-CAP-NOT-INDEPENDENCE-v1. Does not refute QFORM-FULL.
